invariants: The distribution slot occurs twice inside the summand -- once as the weight and once inside the logarithm. That repetition is the whole definition: it is what makes this an *expected* log-probability rather than a sum of unrelated terms, and it is what distinguishes this skeleton from cross_entropy's, where the two positions hold different slots.

The scale slot is a fixed constant, not a free parameter: it only selects units (bits, nats, hartleys, joules per kelvin). Every claim about entropy is therefore invariant to it up to a positive factor.
Non-negative, and zero exactly on point masses; maximized at the uniform distribution, where it equals LOG(N) -- see infotheory.entropy.uniform_entropy.
Concave in the distribution and invariant under relabelling of the alphabet: entropy sees the multiset of probabilities, never the symbols carrying them.

Additive over independent components, which is the property that forces the logarithm: Shannon's axioms (continuity, monotonicity in N, and the grouping/additivity law) determine this functional up to the scale constant.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Entropy is the negated, unit-scaled average of the logarithm of a distribution's own probabilities: the mean number of symbols needed to name an outcome drawn from it.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The corpus's information/thermodynamics bridge. Its typed skeleton `?0:V = neg(*(?1:P, sum⟨*(?2:V, LOG⟨?2:V⟩)⟩))` is shared character for character with physics.thermodynamics.gibbs_entropy, and the two templates are authored deliberately identical modulo slot names because the claim is identity, not resemblance: the same functional of the same kind of object, with kB in the slot where information theory puts 1/ln 2. Unlike the exponential twins that link compounding money to decaying nuclei -- analogies between unrelated subject matters -- this twin has a physical exchange rate attached to it. Landauer's bound prices one bit of erased information at kB*T*ln 2 joules, so the constant occupying the P slot is what converts between the two readings rather than what separates them.
regularity_conditions: A countable alphabet with a proper probability distribution
Terms with p_i = 0 are read as 0 via the limit x*log(x) -> 0
A fixed base, i.e. a fixed value of the scale constant, throughout an argument
failure_modes: The differential-entropy analogue for continuous variables is not a limit of this quantity -- it can be negative and is not invariant under change of variables -- so the discrete intuitions transfer only through relative entropy.

Entropy is a property of a distribution, not of a string. Calling a particular observed sequence 'high entropy' conflates this with Kolmogorov complexity, which is a different (and uncomputable) quantity.
Estimating H from finite samples by plugging in empirical frequencies is biased downward, badly so when the alphabet is large relative to the sample.

Upper bound as well as special case: H <= k*LOG(N) for every distribution on N symbols, with equality exactly at the uniform one, so this node doubles as the extremal statement.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: When every outcome is equally likely, the entropy is just the logarithm of how many outcomes there are, scaled to the chosen units.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The specialization that makes the physics twin concrete: substituting p_i = 1/N into Shannon entropy turns `-(k * sum_i p_i*LOG(p_i))` into `k * LOG(N)`, and the corresponding substitution in physics.thermodynamics.gibbs_entropy turns Gibbs into Boltzmann's S = kB ln W. One derivation, run in two disciplines, arriving at two formulas that are usually taught in different buildings. Structurally it is also the corpus's cleanest instance of a slot disappearing under specialization: the summation and the repeated weight slot both vanish, leaving a scaled logarithm of a count.

All outcomes carry probability exactly 1/N
Same base convention as the entropy it specializes
failure_modes: Read as a definition of entropy it is Hartley's measure, which ignores probabilities entirely and overstates the uncertainty of every non-uniform source.
For countably infinite alphabets there is no uniform distribution, so the bound has no maximizer and entropy can be infinite.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The information carried by an outcome is the negative logarithm of its probability: rarer outcomes tell you more.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The corpus's quietest cross-discipline twin, and one that was predicted before it was checked. Its typed skeleton `?0:V = neg(LOG⟨?1:V⟩)` is identical to chemistry.acid_base.ph_definition's -- pH is literally the surprisal of a proton, quoted in decimal digits instead of bits. The twin is *typed*, not merely shape-level, because both corpora independently declared their two slots `variable`; had either treated the argument as a parameter the match would have degraded. What the pair shows is that the negated-log-of-a-probability form is doing the same work in both places: compressing a multiplicative, many-orders-of-magnitude quantity onto an additive scale a human can hold in mind.
regularity_conditions: p strictly positive; the surprisal of an impossible outcome is +infinity by convention
A fixed logarithm base throughout an argument
failure_modes: Surprisal is a property of an outcome under an assumed model. Reporting a large surprisal as 'this event was informative' when the model itself is wrong measures the model, not the world.
For continuous variables -log of a density is not information: it carries units and can be negative.

functionals.description: Shannon entropy of the joint distribution of its arguments; with two arguments it is the joint entropy H(X, Y). Written as a call rather than expanded so that the additive decomposition of mutual information is visible as structure.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The information two variables share is what their entropies count twice: add the separate uncertainties and subtract the joint uncertainty.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: An additive decomposition whose structure is the same double-counting correction that appears whenever a measure is applied to overlapping objects. Written this way it does *not* twin with settheory.cardinality.inclusion_exclusion_two_sets, because the matcher reads call heads literally and this node's left-hand side is a bare slot rather than a measure applied to a join. That near miss is the reason the companion node infotheory.mutualinfo.entropy_inclusion_exclusion exists: it states the same fact in the CARD/MEET/JOIN vocabulary and the twin then fires exactly. Keeping both is deliberate -- one is how the definition is written in every textbook, the other is what it is.
regularity_conditions: Discrete variables with a well-defined joint distribution
All three entropies finite
Same logarithm base in all three terms
failure_modes: Zero mutual information means independence, not absence of structure that a particular model can use; and estimated mutual information is positively biased, so 'nonzero' from data is weak evidence of dependence.
The three-variable analogue (interaction information) can be negative, so the inclusion-exclusion reading is a signed measure and not a measure of a set of points.

structural_signature.anonymized_template: CARD(JOIN(FIRST, SECOND)) = CARD(FIRST) + CARD(SECOND) - CARD(MEET(FIRST, SECOND))
invariants: The measure of a join is the sum of the measures minus the measure of the meet: finite additivity plus a correction for the shared part. Nothing in the statement is specific to entropy, which is exactly why it twins with the counting version.

CARD here is Yeung's I-measure mu*, which is finitely additive but *signed*: unlike cardinality it can assign a negative value to an atom once three or more variables are involved. Two variables is precisely the range where the set picture is safe.
The overlap term CARD(MEET(.,.)) is mutual information; the meet of independent variables has measure zero, which is the information-theoretic reading of disjointness.
Symmetric in the two operands, and the argument order follows the convention fixed by scripts/seed_logic.py so the twin is exact.

functionals.description: Yeung's I-measure mu*: the signed measure on the field generated by the variables' sigma-algebras with mu*(X~) = H(X). The same head the set-theory corpus uses for cardinality, on purpose -- inclusion-exclusion for counts and for entropies is one theorem about finitely additive measures.

functionals.description: Greatest lower bound. Realized as intersection of information atoms here, as conjunction in data/logic and as set intersection in data/set_theory.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Joint entropy is the sum of the two entropies minus the information they share, the same correction that counting a union requires.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: An exact typed twin of settheory.cardinality.inclusion_exclusion_two_sets, and the reason it fires is authorial: this node borrows the CARD / MEET / JOIN heads that scripts/seed_logic.py introduced for the Boolean lattice instead of writing H, comma and semicolon. That is a translation, not a disguise -- Yeung's I-measure theorem says there is a signed measure mu* on the field generated by the variables with mu*(Xtilde) = H(X) and mu*(Xtilde inter Ytilde) = I(X;Y), so entropy really is a measure and this really is inclusion-exclusion. The pair with the set-theory node gives the corpus a three-corpus family (sets, logic, information) around one measure-theoretic fact, and it shows the price the matcher extracts: twins fire on notation, so a shared abstraction has to be *adopted* before a genuine shared structure becomes visible.

Two variables only: the signed I-measure admits negative atoms from three variables onward
Same logarithm base throughout
failure_modes: The Venn-diagram intuition breaks at three variables: the triple 'intersection' I(X;Y;Z) can be negative, so no set of points realizes the picture.
mu* is not a probability measure and its atoms are not events; reading CARD as a count of anything is a category error.

invariants: A variational statement, not an evaluation: the channel is fixed and the *input distribution* is free, which is what makes capacity a property of the channel alone.
The objective is concave in the input distribution over a convex (simplex) feasible set, so the maximum is attained and is a global one; Blahut-Arimoto exploits exactly this.
Bounded above by the log of the input alphabet size, since mutual information cannot exceed the input entropy.
Zero exactly for a channel whose output distribution does not depend on the input.

The CAPMAX head is an authoring device, not notation anyone writes: the template grammar has no binder for 'maximize over a family', and an identifier spelled `max_p` would be silently parsed as a prefix big-operator (docs/BACKLOG.md). Consequently this node cannot twin with any optimization elsewhere in the corpus until the grammar grows a real binder -- the structural claim is quarantined inside one opaque call.

functionals.name: supremum over a family
functionals.description: Supremum of the first argument as the second ranges over its admissible family. Introduced because the template grammar has no binder for 'max over input distributions', and because identifiers beginning `max_` are parsed as prefix big-operators. Argument order is fixed: objective first, optimized-over object second.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Capacity is the largest mutual information any input distribution can push through a fixed channel.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The node where the template grammar runs out. Every other statement in this corpus is an expression that could be evaluated once its slots are filled; capacity is a maximization over a function space, and the grammar -- identifiers, arithmetic, calls, one prefix big-operator family, relations -- has no binder to express it. Writing `max_p I(X;Y)` would collide with the `max_` big-operator namespace recorded in docs/BACKLOG.md and would in any case lose the constraint set. The honest workaround is an opaque `CAPMAX(objective, argument)` call with a fixed argument order, which parses cleanly and states the dependency structure while conceding that the *internal* structure of the optimization is invisible to the matcher. That concession is worth recording: it marks the boundary between what this corpus can compare and what it can only name, and it is the strongest argument in the corpus for adding binder syntax.
regularity_conditions: A discrete memoryless channel with a fixed transition law
Input distributions range over the probability simplex on the input alphabet
The supremum is a maximum when the input alphabet is finite
failure_modes: Capacity is an asymptotic promise about arbitrarily long block codes; at finite blocklength the achievable rate falls short by a term in the channel dispersion, so quoting C as an engineering throughput overstates it.
The maximizing input distribution is generally not uniform, and assuming it is understates capacity for asymmetric channels.
Feedback does not increase capacity for memoryless channels but does for channels with memory; transplanting the formula is unsafe.

equivalent_forms.scope_note: The existence half; the inequality characterizes achievable length profiles

equivalent_forms.scope_note: The reading that turns the inequality into the entropy bound

invariants: A budget constraint: each codeword of length l consumes a D^(-l) share of the code space, and the shares cannot exceed the whole.
The relation is `<=`, not `=`, and the slack is real -- codes with strict inequality exist and are simply wasteful.

Both a necessary and a sufficient condition, which is unusual: the inequality is necessary for every uniquely decodable code (McMillan) and sufficient for the existence of a prefix code (Kraft), so it characterizes achievable length profiles exactly.
The exponent slot is negated, which makes the terms decreasing in length; the alphabet size is a constant fixed before the code, not a free parameter.
Substituting the ideal lengths l_i = -log_D(p_i) makes the sum equal 1 exactly, which is how this inequality becomes the entropy lower bound on expected code length.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: The codeword lengths of any uniquely decodable code satisfy a budget constraint, and any lengths satisfying it can be realized by a prefix code.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The corpus's only inequality-rooted node with a big-operator on the left and a bare numeral on the right, which makes its skeleton `sum⟨^(?0:P, neg(?1:V))⟩ <= 1` a singleton so far. That is worth stating plainly: not every node earns a twin, and a corpus that only admitted twinnable statements would be evidence of selection rather than of structure. What the node does supply is the bridge from the entropy definitions to *codes*: read D^(-l_i) as a sub-probability and the inequality becomes the reason expected code length cannot fall below entropy, which is the operational meaning of infotheory.entropy.shannon_entropy.

Finitely or countably many codewords
Lengths are positive integers
failure_modes: The inequality constrains lengths, not the code: satisfying it does not make a *given* code prefix-free, it only guarantees that some code with those lengths is.
Integer lengths mean the entropy bound is generally not attained; the gap is under one symbol per codeword (Shannon-Fano) and vanishes only when the probabilities are D-adic.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Cross-entropy is the average surprisal you incur when the world follows one distribution and your code (or model) was built for another.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: A near miss by design. Its skeleton `?0:V = neg(*(?1:P, sum⟨*(?2:V, LOG⟨?3:V⟩)⟩))` differs from Shannon entropy's only in that the two inner slot positions are filled by different slots, so no twin fires -- and that is the correct answer. The pair is the sharpest demonstration in the corpus that the matcher keys on *slot reuse* and not just on operator shape: the structural difference between measuring your own uncertainty and paying for someone else's model is one repeated placeholder. It is also the point where the corpus touches machine learning, since log loss is this quantity with the empirical distribution in the first slot. That contact is now an edge rather than a remark: ml.objective.token_cross_entropy_loss (scripts/seed_ml.py) states the training loss of a language model with the batch average 1/N in the unit-scale slot this node reserves for 1/ln 2, lands on this typed skeleton character for character, and the two nodes carry reciprocal `equivalent_to` edges. The reciprocity had to be written into both corpora by hand, which is the cross-corpus link friction docs/BACKLOG.md records under Schema.

Same logarithm base as the entropy it is compared with
failure_modes: A model that assigns probability zero to an observed outcome makes the cross-entropy infinite, which is why practical training clips or smooths the model's probabilities.
Cross-entropy is not a distance: it does not vanish when the arguments agree (it equals the entropy there), and it is not symmetric.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Relative entropy is the average log-ratio between two distributions weighted by the first: the extra cost, per symbol, of believing the second when the first is true.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: Structurally the entropy skeleton with the logarithm's argument opened up into a ratio, and semantically the quantity that unifies most of this corpus: entropy is the divergence from the uniform distribution up to a constant, mutual information is the divergence from the joint to the product of marginals, and cross-entropy is this plus the entropy. The physics reading is just as direct -- for a system held away from equilibrium, KL from the actual state to the equilibrium state is the available free energy divided by kB*T, so the same functional that prices a bad code prices a thermodynamic disequilibrium. That is the entropy bridge again, one derivative further along.
regularity_conditions: Absolute continuity: q_i > 0 wherever p_i > 0
Terms with p_i = 0 are read as 0
Both arguments are distributions on the same alphabet
failure_modes: Not symmetric and not a metric; reporting 'the KL distance' between two models without saying which is the reference is meaningless.
Infinite whenever the model gives zero probability to something the truth gives positive probability, so it is unusable as a raw objective against sparse empirical distributions.
The two directions optimize differently -- KL(p||q) is mode-covering, KL(q||p) mode-seeking -- and swapping them silently changes what a fitted model looks like.

equivalent_forms.expression: KL(p || q) >= 0, with equality iff p = q

equivalent_forms.scope_note: The coding reading: no code beats the one built for the true distribution
The proof in one line: Jensen's inequality applied to the convex function -log

invariants: Relational rather than definitional: the top node is `>=` against the numeral 0, so unlike every equation in this corpus the statement is irreversible and carries no output slot at all.
Equality holds exactly when the two distributions coincide, which is what makes relative entropy usable as a discrepancy despite not being a metric.
A one-line consequence of the convexity of -log via Jensen's inequality; the same convexity argument gives the whole f-divergence family its non-negativity, which is Csiszar's generalization.
The sign of the scale constant matters here in a way it does not elsewhere: a negative base constant would flip the inequality, so the constant is implicitly positive.

semantic_interpretation.statement_meaning: Relative entropy is never negative, and vanishes only when the two distributions are identical.
semantic_interpretation.statistical_significance: The theorem that turns the divergence definition into a tool: without it, KL would be an expression rather than a discrepancy. It also underwrites three other nodes here -- mutual information is non-negative because it is a KL, entropy is maximized at the uniform distribution because the gap is a KL, and expected code length cannot beat entropy because the shortfall is a KL against the Kraft sub-distribution. Its epistemic status is `derived` rather than `formal` for exactly that reason: it is proved, in one Jensen step, from the convexity of the logarithm, not posited.
regularity_conditions: Both arguments are distributions on the same alphabet
q_i > 0 wherever p_i > 0
Positive base constant
failure_modes: Equality 'iff p = q' is up to sets of probability zero under p; two distributions differing where p vanishes still give divergence 0.

The inequality says nothing about magnitude, so a small KL does not bound the difference in expectations of unbounded functions; Pinsker's inequality is needed for that and only bounds total variation.
